title: How to Meet an Image Upload Size Limit
description: A step-by-step approach to fitting an image under a kilobyte limit without ignoring required dimensions, format or clarity.
intro: Upload forms often specify both a maximum file size and image dimensions. Getting below the size limit is only part of the job: the result still needs to meet the required format and remain readable.

sections.heading: Check every requirement first
paragraphs: Record the exact maximum size, accepted formats, pixel dimensions, aspect ratio and any colour or background rules. A file can be small enough but still rejected because its dimensions or type are wrong.
Confirm the units too. Kilobytes and kibibytes are often used loosely in upload instructions, so leave a little headroom below the stated ceiling when possible.

sections.heading: Reduce dimensions when appropriate
paragraphs: If the source is much larger than the required display, resize it while preserving its aspect ratio. Avoid enlarging a small original to satisfy dimensions; upscaling does not restore missing detail.
When exact dimensions are required, crop intentionally rather than stretching the picture. Keep a backup before cropping or recompressing.

sections.heading: Target the file size and verify
paragraphs: Use Image Resizer in KB to work toward a target file size. For a form with exact width and height, the Image Resizer can set dimensions, then the Image Compressor can reduce bytes further if needed.

Check the final file size, dimensions and format after export. Open the image and inspect fine details, especially text, faces, logos and edges. Some forms may decode and re-encode uploads, so leave a margin below the maximum.

faq.question: Why is my image still over the limit after resizing?
faq.answer: Dimensions are only one factor. Format, quality, metadata and image complexity affect the final bytes. Compress or convert a copy and check the result.

faq.question: Will lowering quality always reduce size enough?
faq.answer: It often reduces size, but the result varies. Use gradual changes and inspect visual quality instead of choosing the most aggressive setting immediately.

faq.question: Should I crop or resize?
faq.answer: Resize to change overall dimensions while keeping the composition. Crop when the required aspect ratio differs and some edges can be removed.

faq.question: How can I avoid being just over the limit?
faq.answer: Aim below the maximum rather than exactly at it, then check the exported file's reported size and the destination's own validation.
